record.paper_title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2
record.original_question: For coprime integers p and q satisfying p > q >= 2, and for a positive real number alpha, what analogous questions and theory can be developed for the fractional parts of the products alpha times (p/q)^n for n = 0, 1, 2, ...?

evidence.quote: Naturally, one can consider analogous problems for the products alpha(p/q)^n (n = 0, 1, 2, ...) where alpha is again a positive number, and p and q are integers satisfying p > q >= 2, (p,q) = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime integers with $p > q \geq 2$, and let $\alpha$ be a positive real number. Consider the sequence of fractional parts
$$\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}, \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
where $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$. Develop a theory analogous to the classical case $(p,q) = (3,2)$ for this sequence. In particular, address the following questions:

(a) For which $\alpha > 0$ is the sequence $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}$ equidistributed modulo $1$?

(b) Define $\Omega(p/q) = \inf_{\alpha > 0}\left(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} - \liminf_{n\to\infty}\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}\right)$. Determine or bound $\Omega(p/q)$.

(c) Does there exist a positive real number $\alpha$ such that $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} < 1/q$ for all $n \geq 0$ (a "$(p/q)$-analogue" of a $Z$-number)? More generally, for which subintervals $I \subset [0,1)$ of length less than $1$ does there exist $\alpha > 0$ with $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} \in I$ for every $n$?

(d) Describe the set of $\alpha > 0$ for which the orbit $\{\alpha(p/q)^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ avoids a prescribed subinterval of $[0,1)$.
artifact.category_tag: Distribution mod 1 of powers of rationals
artifact.status_search_result: The rational-base generalization of Mahler's 3/2-problem remains open. Partial results are known: Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington proved $\Omega(p/q) > 1/q$ for coprime $p > q \geq 2$, and recent work (e.g., arXiv:2411.03468, 2024) establishes that no integer $\alpha$ is a $Z$-number, but the full theory for general $\alpha > 0$ and arbitrary coprime $p/q$ — including existence of $(p/q)$-analogues of Z-numbers and equidistribution questions — is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Mahler's 3/2 problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Mahler conjectured in 1968 that there are no Z-numbers. The existence of Z-numbers remains an open problem. Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington showed that Ω(p/q) > 1/q for rational p/q.
status_evidence.claim: Generalization to p/q remains open with only partial bounds known.

status_evidence.title: Mahler's 3/2 problem in Z^+
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work proving no Z-numbers exist among positive integers, partial progress toward Mahler's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress; full conjecture and its rational-base generalization unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the fractional parts of rational powers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n} for coprime p>q≥2.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on the rational-base generalization continues.
